sentences.text:
Heard Sri Vinay Saran, learned Senior Counsel assisted by Sri Mohammad Alam and Sri P.K.Mishra, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri R.K.Singh, learned A.G.A. in Bail Application No.
33490 of 2019.
None present on behalf of applicants in other connected cases.

2. The applicants have approached this Court by way of filing the present Criminal Misc. Bail Application seeking enlargement on bail in Case Crime No.43 of 2019, under Sections 376-D, 504,
506, 120-B I.P.C., and 3/4 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act 2012 and 3 (2) (5) of SC/ST Act, Police Station-Bilariaganj, District-Azamgarh.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 3. Above referred all the three applicants are facing trial for the offence of gang rape of a minor girl.
According to records, all the three applicants were granted interim bail by this Court vide order dated 29.11.2019 for a limited period of three months.

4. Learned Senior Counsel appearing on behalf of applicant Hannan fairly submits that he has no instructions as to whether applicants have surrendered or not after the period of three months was over.

5. In pursuance of an order passed by this Court, learned Trial Court has submitted a status report that there are 12 proposed prosecution witnesses, however, till date not a single witness has been examined.
It is also informed that due to absence of applicants, statement of P.W.1 is not recorded till date.
From the report it appears that applicants have not appeared before learned Trial Court.

6. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that according to records all the applicants are languishing in jail since 24.3.2019 and 17.6.2019 respectively and there is no likelihood of early disposal of trial.

7. Learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the bail application and submitted that it is a case of gang rape of a minor girl and there are specific allegations against the applicants in the statement of victim recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. as well as they have not followed directions passed while granting interim bail Hannan vs State Of U.P. on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43676908/
2 8.

I have considered the above mentioned rival submissions in referred factual and legal background and in view of established principle of jurisprudence of bail i.e 'bail is rule and jail is exception' as well as relevant factors for consideration of a bail application such as (i) whether there is any prima facie or reasonable ground to believe that the accused had committed the offence; (ii) nature and gravity of the accusation; (iii) severity of the punishment in the event of conviction; (iv) danger of the accused absconding or fleeing, if released on bail; (v) character, behaviour, means, position and standing of the accused;(vi) likelihood of the offence being repeated; (vii) reasonable apprehension of the witnesses being influenced; (viii) danger of course, of justice being thwarted by grant of bail etc. and that an order to grant or not to grant bail must assigned reasons (see Deepak Yadav Vs.
State of U.P. (2022) 8 SCC 559, Manoj Kumar Khokar Vs. State of Rajasthan and Anr (2022) 3 SCC 501, The State of Jharkhand Vs. Dhananjay Gupta @ Dhananjay Prasad Gupta: Order dated 7.11.2023 in SLP (Crl) No.10810/2023 and Shiv Kumar Vs The State of U.P. and Ors: Order dated 12.9.2023 in Criminal Appeal No.2782 of 2023), therefore, I am of considered opinion that present is not a fit case to grant bail to applicant mainly on following reasons:-
(i) Court is of the considered opinion that since applicants have not surrendered after a period of three months as prescribed by order dated 29.11.2019 when interim bail was granted and due to their default, trial is not proceeding, therefore, at this stage no case of bail is made out.

sentences.text: (ii) Court also takes note of statement of victim recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. wherein there are specific allegations against all applicants of committing rape.

9. All the three bail applications are rejected and it is directed that in case applicants have still not surrendered, they will surrender before learned Trial Court within a period of one week and in default, learned Trial Court will have liberty to take all coercive measures for their arrest and for that Police Officers of concerned police station are also directed to take all legal and permissible steps and report thereof shall be submitted to the Registrar General of this Court which shall be kept in the records of these bail applications.
